Application Materials.content:
On the application form, applicants need to give:
- the name and contact details of an academic referee from your current or most recent place of study or a professional referee, if you don't have an academic referee from the last 10 years
- your [personal statement](https://www.bath.ac.uk/guides/writing-a-personal-statement-to-apply-for-a-masters-course/), explaining your reasons for wishing to study the course
- your supporting information
Supporting information required includes:
- a scan of your undergraduate degree certificate and your postgraduate degree certificate, if you have one
- a scan of your final degree transcript or your most recent transcript if you are still studying
- an academic reference from your current or most recent place of study, if you have one or a professional reference if you don't have an academic reference available from the last 10 years
- an up-to-date CV
You can also [upload supporting documents through Application Tracker](https://www.bath.ac.uk/services/application-tracker-for-postgraduate-taught-courses/) after you have submitted your online application. You do not need to have all these documents ready to submit at the point of making your initial application.
International applicants should also give:
- an authorised translation of your degree certificate and transcript if they are not in English
- your English language test certificate, if available

Application Deadlines.content:
- Home application deadline: **31 August 2026**. We recommend you apply early as we may close applications before the deadline if a course is full.
- Overseas application deadline: **30 June 2026**. We recommend you apply early as we may close applications before the deadline if a course is full. We may consider late applications but if you need a Student Visa to study in the UK, you will need time to apply for and receive your visa to be in the UK by the start of the course.

Academic Requirements.content:
- To apply for this course, you should have an undergraduate degree equivalent to **2:2 to 2:1 or above depending on the institution attended**.
- Your degree can be in any discipline but you must have studied a subject with high quantitative content. You will be better suited to this course if you have studied business or management, or studied a subject with high quantitative content, such as:
- mathematics/statistics
- computer science
- engineering
- physics
- a quantitative social science
- If you are a UK student and completed your undergraduate degree abroad, your qualification must be equivalent to **a 2:2 to 2:1 or above depending on the institution attended**.
- Previous experience of computer programming is an advantage. You should include information about your quantitative and programming experience in your personal statement.
- In exceptional cases, relevant work experience may be a substitute for the degree requirement. You should have **no more than three years’ relevant work experience**.
- For applicants with Chinese qualifications: **A four year Bachelor degree with a final overall score of at least 62-75% depending on the institution attended**.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
You will need an International English Language Test System (IELTS) score of **at least 6.5 overall**. Your scores for reading, writing, listening and speaking **must be at least 6.0**. These results must be no more than two years old from the start date of your MSc course. [Read more on the IELTS website](https://www.ielts.org/).
We also accept other language tests, including PTE Academic, TOEFL. iBT, CPE and CAE. [Read more about alternative language tests](https://www.bath.ac.uk/corporate-information/postgraduate-taught-courses-english-language-requirements-for-international-students/).
If you have already taken a test but have not met the required standard, you can apply to take a pre-sessional course at the University. [Find out more about pre-sessional courses](https://www.bath.ac.uk/guides/choosing-your-pre-sessional-course/).
If you completed all of your undergraduate studies in:
- the UK
- a country where English is the official first language
You may be exempt from our English language requirements.
If you have an overall IELTS score of 6.0 or 5.5 you may qualify for a combined offer.
- Five-week course: An overall IELTS score of **6.0** may allow you to take a five-week English course before your MSc. Each of your listening, reading, writing and speaking scores must be **at least 5.5**.
- Ten-week course: An overall IELTS score of **5.5** may allow you to take a ten-week course before your MSc. Each of your listening, reading, writing and speaking scores must be **at least 5.5**.
[Find out more about combined offers](https://www.bath.ac.uk/guides/choosing-your-pre-sessional-course/).

Program Overview.content:
Develop your understanding of business analytics. You’ll graduate with the skills you need to start a career specialising in data and decision analysis. This course is for graduates who want to pursue a career in business analytics. The course teaches how companies can use ‘big data’ to gain business insight and how to convert data into knowledge. Students get hands-on practical experience using the latest business intelligence software and interpreting real data.
This course includes guest lectures from industry experts, and a unit co-delivered by a specialist from IBM. It is in partnership with IBM, Qlik, WinPure and [the Women in OR & Analytics Network](https://www.theorsociety.com/get-involved/society-groups/special-interest-groups-and-networks/women-in-or-analytics-network/).
- An MSc in Business Analytics gives you a range of career opportunities across different sectors.
- Students get practical experience in computer programming and the latest business analytics software.
- Small, carefully-selected class sizes allow for plenty of individual interaction with academics, career advisors and industry experts.
- Graduates are equipped with the skills global employers want; big data's importance to businesses is growing, and graduates are in high demand.
- A dissertation based on real data might allow you to work with a partner company. [Watch Business Analytics students share their experience of doing an industrial dissertation](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LYcI9L6r07w).
- Meetings with graduates, business challenges and careers fairs give experience of the global job market.
The MSc in Business Analytics is ranked top 100 in the world and UK top 10 in the [QS Business Masters rankings 2026](https://www.topuniversities.com/business-masters-rankings/business-analytics).
The School combines the latest research with opportunities to apply it. Students develop key professional skills and work with partner organisations on optional projects from day one. Graduates have a great employment record; most go on to careers in a range of areas, start their own business or begin a PhD. 81% of 2022 and 2023 graduates had accepted a job offer within three months of completing their degree.
[The School of Management building opened in June 2022](https://www.bath.ac.uk/campaigns/the-school-of-managements-home/). The latest technology provides a flexible and modern learning environment, with an open layout to enable teamwork and a dedicated Employability Hub for meeting and networking with industry partners.
Students learn from staff with backgrounds and expertise in relevant areas of business analytics. The course has been designed so the available units complement each other to meet its overall aims. Timetabled contact hours, made up of lectures, seminars, tutorials and laboratory classes, are typically between 10 and 16 hours a week during the taught semesters. Additional briefing sessions support preparation for the dissertation period and live projects. Students receive direct guidance from an allocated member of academic staff for dissertation activity. Independent learning and assessment is typically around 25 - 30 hours per week.
Assessment includes individual and group assignments, examinations, written submissions, live presentations and recorded videos. Assessment is designed to support professional development in important business skills. The final degree grade is determined by a weighted average of the taught semesters (two thirds) and the dissertation/practice activity (one third).

Curriculum.content:
- Course title: Business Analytics
- Final award: MSc
- Mode of study: Full-time
- Location: University of Bath, Claverton Down, Bath BA2 7AY
Units include:
- Business statistics and forecasting: 10 credits
- Databases and business intelligence: 10 credits
- Optimisation and spreadsheet modelling: 10 credits
- Analytics in practice: 5 credits
- Data mining and machine learning: 10 credits
- Heuristics and simulation: 10 credits
Optional units:
- Advanced business forecasting: 5 credits
- Advanced data visualisation: 5 credits
- Operations strategy: 5 credits
- Project management: 5 credits
- Dissertation in business analytics: 30 credits
Dissertation in business analytics: **30 credits**. Complete a written research project. You'll find a business analytics problem in an area that interests you, investigate the problem using an existing technique or by developing your own method, come up with a way to solve the problem, interpret your results, derive insights from them and suggest courses of action, and have the chance to work on a real analytics challenge set by one of our industrial partners.
Timetabled contact hours, which can be made up of lectures, seminars, tutorials and laboratory classes, vary throughout your course and between courses but are typically between 10 and 16 hours a week during the taught semesters. Additional briefing sessions will be provided to help you prepare for the dissertation period and as part of the co-curricular offering of live projects. You will receive direct guidance from an allocated member of academic staff for your dissertation activity.
As well as timetabled contact hours, you're expected to undertake independent learning and assessment. Typically, this might be around 25 - 30 hours per week, and include individual research, reading journal articles and books, working on individual and group projects, preparing coursework, presentations, or revising for exams.
Assessment includes individual and group assignments, as well as examinations. The work required may include written submissions, live presentations and recorded videos. The final degree grade is determined by a weighted average of the taught semesters (two thirds) and the dissertation/practice activity (one third).

Cost of Attendance.content:
Postgraduate sample expenditure budget 2026-2027 (52 weeks). This budget does not include tuition fees, flights home or visa charges.
- Rent: Postgraduate University Managed ranges from £173-£503 per week; average costs - £286 p/w. Postgraduate Privately Managed ranges from £217-£391 per week. Rent - Off Campus Bath averages £800 per month, bills not inclusive.
- Food, Toiletries, Household goods: £50 per week.
- Utility Bills (gas, water, electricity), off campus accommodation only: £41 per week.
- Clothes: £16 per week.
- Travel, local & outside of Bath (public transport): £17 per week.
- Leisure/Social/Sport: £25 per week.
- Mobile Phone: £3 per week.
- Health Costs (e.g. Contact lenses, Dentist, Prescriptions etc): £5 per week.
- Course costs (books, materials, photocopying, printing & equipment etc.; these can vary depending on the course so check with your Department): £10 per week.
- Laptop: £650.
- Total Weekly Cost (post graduate in halls of residence): £453.
- Total Costs Per Academic Year - including laptop: £24,206.

Application deadlines:
- Courses starting September 2026: **apply by 4 February 2026** for a decision by **27 February 2026**; **apply by 8 April 2026** for a decision by **8 May 2026**. Applications for scholarships open December 2025. Offer holders can [apply for scholarships through Application Tracker](https://www.bath.ac.uk/services/application-tracker-for-postgraduate-taught-courses/).
- Courses starting in January 2027: apply by **1 October 2026** for a decision by 30 October 2026; apply by **2 November 2026** for a decision by 30 November 2026. Applications for scholarships open in September 2026. Offer holders can [apply for scholarships through Application Tracker](https://www.bath.ac.uk/services/application-tracker-for-postgraduate-taught-courses/).
School scholarships are scholarships you can apply for with varying amounts up to £15,000 available to offer holders from UK, Europe and overseas. To be considered for one of the School of Management Taught Postgraduate full-time Master's Scholarships, you **must** have received an offer to study one of the eligible Taught Postgraduate Master’s courses in the School of Management for the relevant entry year, applied for a scholarship within one of the scholarship application deadlines relevant to the course start date, and applied using the correct application form for the scholarship you are applying for. If awarded a scholarship, the money will be taken off your tuition fee. You do not have to pay it back.
Other scholarships include:
- GREAT Scholarships 2026: 1 x £15,000 for a student from Nigeria; 1 x £10,000 for a student from Pakistan; 1 x £10,000 for a student from Greece; 1 x £10,000 for a student from Spain. Available to students starting their course in September. [Find out more about GREAT Scholarships](https://www.bath.ac.uk/campaigns/great-scholarships-2026/).
- Sir Jack Cater scholarship: £3,000 for a graduate of nominated Hong Kong universities, available to a student starting their course in September. [Find out more about the Sir Jack Cater scholarship](https://www.bath.ac.uk/campaigns/sir-jack-cater-scholarship/).
- CMA CGM Excellence Fund for Education: full-tuition fee waiver and stipend, supported by shipping and logistics company CMA CGM Group, available to students starting their course in September. [Find out more about the CMA CGM Exellence Fund for Education](https://www.bath.ac.uk/campaigns/cma-cgm-excellence-fund-for-education/).
- Discretionary Scholarship: Admissions for MSc full-time courses in the School of Management from time to time may apply a discretionary scholarship at the time of offer to new applicants deemed to be demonstrating high level entry requirements and exceptional application for the course applied for. This award allocation is discretionary and may not be allocated to all applicants. If awarded, the details will be included at the time of offer. The discretionary scholarship is applied as a tuition fee waiver up to the value of £5,000.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: If you have accepted your place and paid the course deposit but want to defer entry to the next academic year, contact the MSc Admissions Team at [mscadmissions-som@bath.ac.uk](mailto:mscadmissions-som@bath.ac.uk).

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
If you have already taken a test but have not met the required standard, you can apply to take a pre-sessional course at the University. [Find out more about pre-sessional courses](https://www.bath.ac.uk/guides/choosing-your-pre-sessional-course/).
Combined offers: if you have an overall IELTS score of **6.0 or 5.5** you may qualify for a combined offer.
- Five-week course: an overall IELTS score of **6.0** may allow you to take a five-week English course before your MSc. Each of your listening, reading, writing and speaking scores must be at least **5.5**.
- Ten-week course: an overall IELTS score of **5.5** may allow you to take a ten-week course before your MSc. Each of your listening, reading, writing and speaking scores must be at least **5.5**.
[Find out more about combined offers](https://www.bath.ac.uk/guides/choosing-your-pre-sessional-course/).
